And I remember that the bus that was there, they couldn't turn the engine on, so they all started pushing the bus and then got into the bus, and together with this other vehicle that I was in, we were taken all together to the Vukovar barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I see. Where did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I spent the night at the Vukovar barracks, in a room there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And what happened the next morning?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: The next morning, on the 22nd of November, 1991, we were, all of us, put on a bus which was a kind of two-part bus and we were taken to Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And where in Sremska Mitrovica? Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Sremska Mitrovica is in Serbia. It is quite close to the border. I was put up in one of the premises in the prison which is actually a civilian prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I see. So you were in prison. How long did you stay in prison?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: I was there for exactly six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Six months. And what happened?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: There was an exchange and I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Where did you go after the exchange? What was your destination?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: I went to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And once you reached Zagreb did you continue to take part in combat operations; and if so, in which?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: I was on sick-leave for about three or four months and then I returned to the Dubrovnik theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: So you took part in other operations?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was a member of the 1st Guards Brigade. I was a professional soldier and I took part in all other operations that my unit participated in, including the Dubrovnik theatre of war, the hinterland of Zadar for two years. I took part in the Operations Lightning and Storm -- Flash and Storm, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: When you came to testify for the first time, do you remember whether you travelled with other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And did you discuss the contents of your testimony with these other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Not the contents. We spoke about the events that we had witnessed. We discussed these things amongst ourselves but not really the contents of my testimony. I didn't talk about it and they didn't talk about it with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. We are approaching the last question. Before your testimony in 1996 you were in contact with the military security services in Zagreb, were you?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. As a professional military man of Croatia I couldn't go anywhere abroad without my superior in Croatia knowing about it. So as an officer it was my duty to report leaving and going to a foreign country, and I had to let them know why. That was the normal procedure. But I wish to say something. It is important to note that this happened just before my first arrival here to testify. Before that in 1992, 1993, 1994, I never discussed this with anyone. I made my statement only once in the office of the President of the republic, Dr. Franjo Tudjman, and that was in 1992. That was my story, actually. I recounted what had happened to me. Regarding the statement in the office of the President of the republic is something I probably didn't mention in my earlier testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: I see. When you had this contact with the military security service, did they tell you what you should say in the Tribunal regarding your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: You see, first of all, my story didn't need any kind of additions because from the beginning I said that I only wanted to tell the truth. My attitude towards the whole story is clear and this can be seen from my going to Belgrade and testifying in favour of a man who was a member of the enemy forces. I'm sorry that I didn't manage to liberate both of them. I did manage to free only one. And I would never have allowed anyone to influence my story or to tell me what I should say, because it's bad enough as it is, because lies would be discovered sooner or later and I would not have liked that to have happened. So I never received any suggestions as to what I should say, never from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a last question, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the last one, because we need to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, does the name Colonel Ivankovic mean anything to you; and if so what?

utterances.speaker: VILIM KARLOVIC
utterances.text: While we were standing in front of the hangar, a woman came in front of the hangar and she was wailing and crying, saying that her son, who was an invalid, was in the hangar. And she was asking this JNA officer to bring her son out and he took her in and they brought out the young man. She said that he was retarded, that he was not well. And when this woman and her son were leaving, I remember that this man said, "Remember that your son's life was saved by," and then there are several surnames which are similar and I'm not sure which one it was; was it Ivankovic, Ivanovic, or Jovanovic? These three surnames are similar and I seem to remember them. The words were: "Remember that your son's life was saved by," and then one of these three surnames was mentioned. I can't remember which.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President. Just a point of clarification. Regarding the video that we saw with the flag - you will remember that - I have been told that the video was made by Adno Verlinden in Vukovar for SkyNews, so the information I gave was wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Sir, your examination-in-chief has just been completed. You will come back tomorrow for the cross-examination. As now you're a witness of justice, you will no longer be able to contact the Office of the Prosecutor and you mustn't discuss what you have said with anyone, including any witnesses that may be staying in the same hotel as you. So you can talk about the rain, the weather, but not about the case. And you will come back here tomorrow at 8.30 because that is when we begin the hearing. So I'll ask Madam Usher to escort you out. I wish to touch upon two other issues with Mr. Seselj before we adjourn, so you may leave now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, first issue. You asked for proof that Madam Raguz was informed. I wish to show you two documents which show that Madam Raguz was informed on the 3rd of March, at 4.52 in the afternoon, of the fact that the proceedings will be viva voce. There's an e-mail sent by the officer of the Chamber to Ms. Marina Raguz. And also a copy of the same was sent to the registrar of the case and other individuals from the Tribunal. I will provide this for you. A second document. On Monday, at 12.16, Madam Raguz again was told that the Chamber had rendered a decision and that the Prosecutor and you yourself would have two hours, 30 minutes, for the questions. So here are the two documents which we are going to give you. They are in English, but I think that you have some knowledge of the language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the 3rd of March is not indicated anywhere here. There's no 3rd of March. This is an English method of writing - though I don't know any English, but I hear a word or two - this is the English way of writing first the month and then the day. So when it says "3/10," it is not the 3rd of March but the 10th of March. That was what was sent yesterday to Marina Raguz. And the other document of the 7th of March, you know that that was last Monday. After that there was Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. All three days we were here in the courtroom, and all these three days you were telling me that Vilim Karlovic would be testifying under 92 ter and I was complaining about it. So you see, your information is not quite correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, do not add any confusion. I wish to confirm, because I was a witness of this, that last week, on Friday, Madam Raguz was informed, and you have the proof of it in front of you. And Monday, the 10th of March, Madam Raguz again received information that you would have two and a half hours, as well as the Prosecutor. That is what was done. And who sent the information is front of you -- in front of me, so please don't call in question the people who have done everything they could for you to be informed in a timely fashion. Madam Raguz was informed on Friday and on Monday. So we are going to further improve the method of information. We will make sure that you will be the one to receive without any delay this type of information, and we are working on this so as to avoid this type of problem. Second point I wish to make: The Chamber, which discussed the matter a moment ago, has decided that the next witness who will come on Thursday, Mr. Berghofer, will be heard under the procedure of Rule 92 ter. As a result the Chamber gives the Prosecutor already now 30 minutes for the presentation of the written and consolidated statement, dated the 6th of March, 2008. There are five documents which will be shown, photographs and maps. And, Mr. Seselj, you will have one and a half hours to cross-examine. The testimony of Mr. Berghofer will complete the testimony of the witness that we heard today and that we had in front of us. It is Tuesday today. You have all of tomorrow to prepare for the cross-examination. If you do not wish to ask questions under the cross-examination, then the Chamber will ask questions and the testimony of this witness will be completed on Thursday. That is what I wanted to tell you. We have three more minutes left. If you wish to take the floor, I will gladly give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Are you going to explain to me, Judge, that this is possible? If you, as a Trial Chamber, ruled yesterday that Witness Vilim Karlovic should be heard viva voce, how is it possible that the Registry could inform Marina Raguz on Friday about it? The decision was made yesterday for Vilim Karlovic to be heard viva voce. And secondly, why would the secretariat have to go by Belgrade to inform me about this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you straight away. On Friday I was in contact with the office of the Chamber and with my colleagues and we decided that it would be viva voce, and I gave instructions that you should be immediately informed of this through the intermediary of Madam Raguz. Also, we rendered a decision, a written decision which consists of several pages, to specify the transfer from 92 ter to viva voce. As the written decision needs to be registered and translated, this was only done on Monday. And it is an order to give you time that we informed you about this on Friday, not to place you in a position of a fait accomplis. So you see, on the part of the Chamber, a maximum of effort was invested to inform you. Maybe we did too much. Maybe we needn't have done so much. We could have waited for Monday to tell you. But surely you're not going to reproach us for this. That would be really too much. We wanted to give you all the information in due time. We could have waited until Monday for the decision to be recorded and communicated to you. I wanted you to be informed several days in advance, that is as of Friday. If Madam Raguz, and I can understand that she may not have received the message and was unable to convey it to you, fine. We are going to remedy this and we will make sure that you receive the information directly. It is true that if you had a Defence counsel, the question would not arise. We would have immediately informed counsel and he would have prepared himself. It so happens that you are acting as your own counsel. We thought that your assistants are constantly in touch with you, and informing them they would automatically inform you, because of course there is telephone communication between Belgrade and The Hague. This was not done. We will make sure that in future you will have no cause for criticism. But you must know that the desire of the Chamber was to inform you as soon as possible. That is what I wanted to tell you, Mr. Seselj. It is time to adjourn. My colleagues have to work in another proceeding in a few minutes. We'll meet again tomorrow at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just ten seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can contact my associates by telephone only when I call them and in no other way. During the weekend Marina Raguz cannot contact me through the detention authorities because the officer in the management of the detention centre is not working during the weekend. And thirdly, for the five years, all information, all decisions and all documents were handed over to me and I had to sign for it. I have to sign everything I receive. So please do not inform anyone else. When Marina Raguz is on trial, then you can send her the information. Marina Raguz doesn't exist for you. She cooperates with me and not with you. She has nothing to do with this Tribunal as the question of her funding has not been resolved. She has no -- there's no reason to contact her. I am the counsel here and as the counsel I have to be informed like all other counsel. And you know my address and it hasn't changed for the past five years. So why look for me via Addis Ababa or Palma de Mallorca. Why don't they look for me in Scheveningen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have taken note of what you have said, and of course also the point that it is not possible to communicate with you during the weekend. As I said we will meet again tomorrow at 8.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of March, 2008, at 8.30 a.m. 21 22 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.16 p.m.,
